theory.intro: Right pyramids and right cones have a **perpendicular height** $h$ that drops straight from the apex to the centre of the base. For a right square pyramid, the **face slant height** $l$ is the distance from the apex to the midpoint of a base edge; for a right cone, $l$ runs from the apex down the sloping surface to the base circumference. Each slant height forms a right-angled triangle with the perpendicular height and a length in the base.
facts: The **slant height** $l$ is the longest of the three lengths, so it is the **hypotenuse** of the right-angled triangle.
If a **diameter** is given for a cone, halve it to get the radius $r$ first.
Take only the **positive** square root, since a length cannot be negative.
steps: Identify the right-angled triangle and label its legs and hypotenuse.
Decide whether the unknown is the hypotenuse (slant height) or a shorter side.
Apply Pythagoras' theorem and take the positive root.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The radius is $r=12\div2=6\text{ m}$. The slant height is the hypotenuse; the perpendicular height is a shorter side.

$\begin{align*}h^{2}+6^{2}&=11^{2}\\h^{2}&=121-36\\h^{2}&=85\\h&=\sqrt{85}\text{ m}\end{align*}$

Half the base edge is $30\div2=15\text{ mm}$. The face slant height is the hypotenuse.

$\begin{align*}h^{2}+15^{2}&=17^{2}\\h^{2}&=289-225\\h^{2}&=64\\h&=8\text{ mm}\end{align*}$

foundation.question_text:
A cone has base radius $8\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $15\text{ cm}$.
Find the slant height $l$.
foundation.solution_text:
The slant height is the hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle.
$l=\sqrt{8^{2}+15^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{289}$
$=17\text{ cm}$

foundation.question_text:
A cone has base radius $12\text{ cm}$ and slant height $20\text{ cm}$.
Find the perpendicular height $h$.
foundation.solution_text:
The perpendicular height is a shorter side of the right-angled triangle.
$h=\sqrt{20^{2}-12^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{256}$
$=16\text{ cm}$

development.question_text:
A cone has base radius $6\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $11\text{ cm}$.
Find the slant height $l$ in exact surd form.
development.solution_text:
The slant height is the hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle.
$l=\sqrt{6^{2}+11^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{157}\text{ cm}$

development.question_text:
The sloping edge of a right square pyramid, running from the apex down to a base corner, is $26\text{ cm}$ long, and the base edge is $20\text{ cm}$.
Find the slant height of a triangular face (the distance from the apex to the midpoint of a base edge).
development.solution_text:
The face slant height, half the base edge and the sloping edge form a right-angled triangle, with the sloping edge as the hypotenuse. Half the base edge is $20\div2=10\text{ cm}$.
$l=\sqrt{26^{2}-10^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{576}$
$=24\text{ cm}$

mastery.solution_text:

$l=\sqrt{7^{2}+24^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{625}$
$=25\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text:
A right square pyramid has base edge $22\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $17\text{ cm}$.
Find the slant height $l$ of a triangular face in exact surd form.
mastery.solution_text:
Half the base edge is $22\div2=11\text{ cm}$; this and the perpendicular height are the two shorter sides.
$l=\sqrt{17^{2}+11^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{410}\text{ cm}$
